thread:
eli: quick sync: i sketched an "autonomous-lease" concept that tries to merge the signed-lease and capability-token ideas into a single, small artifact that runtimes can validate offline. goal: minimal runtime logic, strong audit, workable revocation for private installs.
maria: interested. what makes it different from the other drafts?
eli: three core properties: compact signed claims (like signed-lease), a tiny bounded policy set (model/project/action/quota_bucket) evaluated with a simple match algorithm (not full CEL), and a rev_seq used for light revocation semantics pushed through config-sync.
kevin: so runtime needs to check signature, expiry, scope, and rev_seq <= local_rev_seq?
eli: exactly. if rev_seq is greater than local_rev_seq and runtime is offline, behavior depends on tenant config: conservative -> deny, permissive -> allow-with-audit. default is permissive but logs a high-severity audit event.
sara: we need to be explicit about clock skew. what's allowed for iat/exp?
eli: propose +/- 5s tolerance by default; documentable per-deploy. we can make it configurable per-tenant manifest.
kevin: how about replay attacks? nonce + lease_id should be sufficient; runtimes can maintain a short LRU of recent nonces (configurable memory footprint).
maria: revocation via rev_seq is clever since config-sync already ships state to private installs. but how do operators handle forced immediate revocation if a key is rotated?
eli: two handles: 1) key rotation issues a new root pubkey and increments rev_seq for all active tokens (tokens signed by old key become invalid if rev_seq changed), 2) operators can push a revoke-list snapshot to config-sync for high-security revocations (rare path).
kevin: we should keep the token tiny for network efficiency. what's the wire format? compact JSON then base64-signed? or CBOR?
eli: compact JSON base64-signed v1 to start. later we can move to CBOR if needed. sample payload:
```json
{"lid":"a1","iss":"cp-main","proj":"search","mdl":"rwd-3b","act":"infer","qb":"q42","iat":1759992440,"exp":1759992460,"rev":7,"nonce":"n-7"}
```
ops-bot: rollout checklist: add signer endpoint + key-rotation docs; add verifier lib (go/rust/python); add rev_seq channel to config-sync; add console mapping lid -> reason; perf-test renew traffic.
sara: metrics: need lease-validation latency histogram, reject_reason counters, rev_seq_mismatch events, and renew_rps per-tenant.
maria: fallback routing: token may include fallback_hint so runtime can pick alternative local pool when validation fails. that helps reduce user-visible errors when control plane unreachable.
kevin: compatibility: runtimes accept old probes, new autonomous-lease, and still honor runtime-local routing overrides. feature-flag rollouts required.
eli: security note: do not include prompt content in the token. if we need prompt-sampling for debugging, only include a sampled hashed token that is opt-in.
sara: one more ops constraint: private installs may have strict_revocation flag that flips default to deny-on-unknown. include guidance in RFC.
eli: i'll write up a short RFC with tradeoff matrix (ttl renew vs rev_seq vs full revoke-list), sample verifier pseudo-code, audit event schema, and a rollout plan. i'll post to #rfc by EOD.
maria: +1. can you also stub a unit test plan for runtime libs? kevin can help with perf numbers.
kevin: will add perf test backlog item. :thumbsup:
eli: thanks — i'll ping infra once draft is up.
